newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark to take a breather before 1.80.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr/mark to take a breather before 1.80.

text.p: Dollar/mark may need to take a breather before conquering 1.80 and attaining an objective at 1.8025 later this week, analysts said on Monday.
They noted dollar/mark set another near-six-year high on Tuesday while sterling rallied versus the mark anew for a fresh 81-month high.
"Dollar/mark is in a hefty consolidation after a big run-up," said MCM CurrencyWatch senior analyst Kevin Harris.
In late trading, dollar/mark was quoted at 1.7950/60 versus 1.7895/05 at the open, and dollar/yen at 113.95/05 vs. 113.92/02.
"People are taking profit but there is no effort to push dollar/mark back down. It's safe to say 1.80 mark will be taken out this week," Harris predicted.

Chartists said dollar/mark had a bullish breakout in a six-week rising channel coming in at 1.7940. This pointed to further gains with an objective at 1.8025, just above key psychological resistance at 1.80.

Sterling/mark was equally bullish although it was giving out signals of being slightly overbought which pointed to a near-term consolidation similar to dollar/mark's. However, the 3.00 level was not expected to give way any time soon.
Analysts said the sterling/mark target was in the 3.0575/90 area, the cycle high in October 1990.
The mark's all-around weakness signaled that other big levels could give way soon, such as key supports at 969.50 on mark/lira or 62.85 on mark/yen.
"Mark/yen also got really clubbered," noted Harris who expected the yen to remain well supported by talk the Bank of Japan will eventually hike interest rates.
Dollar/yen remained mostly lackluster in quiet trading, with 114.25 seen as the first main hurdle and 113.25 support likely to hold, chartists said.

In a positive development for the dollar outlook, dollar/Swiss played catch-up with dollar/mark it had lagged lately, chartists said, although they cautioned 1.48 remains a big level to take out on the way to the March high at 1.4922.

Analysts also pointed out that the Irish punt and the French franc were at a near 13-percent divergence within Europe's exchange rate mechanism, closing in on the boundary of the 15-percent ERM band. They said this raised concern mandatory intervention may be triggered this week to curb the rise of the punt that is mirroring sterling/mark.
